From: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@acme.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Clarification on MSA: output ownership, training on customer data, and feedback license

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for the product demo last week — Acme is keen to move toward a pilot but procurement needs clarity on a few IP/data points in the proposed MSA before we can proceed. I attached the relevant RFP excerpt (Section 7). Can you confirm Redwood's position on the following?

1) Output ownership: We need explicit confirmation that all customer-provided prompts, inputs, and the outputs/responses generated by the model when using Acme data are owned by Acme and that Redwood will not assert ownership.
2) Model training/data use: Will Redwood use any customer prompts, outputs, or telemetry to train/redesign models or otherwise incorporate into models that may be served to other customers? If yes, we need opt-in language or an explicit opt-out.
3) Feedback license: If Redwood requests usage of customer interactions/feedback for product improvement, what scope of license are you asking for (derivative rights, sublicensing, timebound)?
4) Auditability & provenance: We need minimal logging/audit trail showing data lineage for compliance reviews — can Redwood provide this and for how long?

Could you loop in legal and let us know what language you can offer? A concise set of proposed clauses would be very helpful.

Best,
Samir Gupta
Sr. Product Manager — AI Platform
Acme Corporation
(samir.gupta@acme.com)

That said, we have several flavors of feedback/license language depending on whether the customer permits model training, allows only aggregated telemetry, or wants a complete opt-out.

I attached the current Redwood MSA draft (v2) so legal can redline against it. Can we get a short redline and proposed language by Wednesday PST? Also propose a 30-minute legal/technical sync tomorrow afternoon if that helps.

Subject: RE: Clarification on MSA: output ownership, training on customer data, and feedback license

Samir / Evelyn — thanks for the clear summary and the draft MSA. I reviewed Acme's RFP excerpt and Redwood's draft and prepared a concise set of recommended redlines and alternative language to cover the four points you raised. High level: Redwood can accept customer ownership of outputs and a narrow, timeboxed feedback license (opt-in) that explicitly excludes training on customer data for third-party-serving models unless separately agreed.

Summary of proposed positions (short):
- Output ownership: Accept as requested. Insert clause: "Customer Output Rights: Customer shall retain all right, title and interest in Customer Data and Outputs. Redwood shall have no ownership interest in such Outputs and shall not assert any rights therein except as expressly set forth in this Agreement."

- Model training / data use: Default position — Redwood will not use Customer Data (including prompts, outputs, or non-anonymized telemetry) to train models intended to be served to other customers. If Customer opts into model improvement, include an explicit, narrow Training Opt-In Addendum that: (a) lists permitted data types, (b) uses only de-identified/aggregated data, (c) is revocable with 30 days' notice, and (d) limits downstream distribution. Proposed clause: "No Training Without Contract: Redwood shall not use Customer Data to train or improve models that are used to serve other customers unless Customer executes a separate Training Opt-In Addendum specifying the scope, de-identification measures, and revocation terms."

- Feedback license: Prefer a limited license for product improvement telemetry only (operational metrics, anonymized aggregates), expressly excluding derivative works and sublicensing. Proposed language: "Feedback License (Limited): Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, royalty-free, worldwide license to use Feedback provided by Customer solely to operate, maintain, and improve Redwood's services, limited to aggregated or de-identified information. This license does not permit Redwood to incorporate Customer Data into models that are made generally available to third parties absent a separate written agreement."

- Auditability & retention: We can provide request-based provenance logs for a rolling 12-month window (subject to reasonable charges for extended retention). Proposed line: "Audit & Data Provenance: Redwood will retain service logs sufficient to demonstrate data lineage for twelve (12) months and make such logs available to Customer upon request under a standard audit process. Extended retention or continuous export can be provided under a separate SOW."

Risk notes / negotiation points to flag:
- Some product telemetry (e.g., failure traces) may contain snippets of prompt text; these must be handled as Customer Data under the MSA. We propose mandatory redaction/de-identification procedures in any Training Opt-In Addendum.
- The feedback license should be narrowly scoped and explicitly time-limited to avoid open-ended rights.

Next steps: I attached a redlined MSA (MSA_Redlines_Acme_v1.docx) with inline edits. If that looks reasonable, let's schedule the 30-min legal call tomorrow 3pm PST or Thursday 10am PST.

Laura Bennett

Laura / Evelyn — thanks for the quick and thorough response. The redline summary aligns with what procurement and our legal team are comfortable with. A few clarifications before we proceed to final redline: 

- On Training Opt-In: Acme's preference is to categorically exclude training on customer prompts/outputs unless we explicitly sign a training addendum. That addendum must be reversible and limited to de-identified telemetry only. Your proposed revocation and de-identification language looks acceptable; please ensure the opt-in requires explicit signature by Acme's legal signatory.

- Feedback License scope: We can accept a limited, non-exclusive license for aggregated telemetry (operational metrics, failure rates, anonymous usage counts) but not for any content-level derivatives. Please remove any language that could be interpreted as allowing Redwood to create derivative models from Acme data.

- Audit logs: We need assurance that the provenance logs will include timestamps and a high-level indicator of whether a given response used any cached material. If 12 months is the default, what is the incremental cost to extend to 24 months?

If you can incorporate these clarifications into a single redline file I can circulate to Acme procurement/legal. Otherwise I'm happy to take your redline and mark up small edits.

Thanks — Samir
